jobTitles.title: Search queries
jobTitles.description: Queries to provide to LinkedIn job search. [It supports boolean operators](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a524335). We will run the scraper once for each query. All filters below will be applied to each query.

locations.title: Locations Filter
locations.description: Filter by these LinkedIn locations. Example: `San Francisco`. LinkedIn does not always understand your text queries. For example for "UK" query it will apply "Ukraine" location, so you should use "United Kingdom" in this case. Try this out first in the location filter input of LinkedIn search at `https://www.linkedin.com/search/results/people/?geoUrn=%5B%22103644278%22%5D`

maxItems.title: Maximum number of jobs to scrape per each job title and location input
maxItems.description: Maximum number of jobs to scrape per each job title and location input.

company.title: Company Filter
company.description: Filter by these companies. Provide full URLs or company names to search in LinkedIn

workplaceType.title: Workplace Type
workplaceType.description: Select one or more applicable workplace types.

employmentType.title: Employment Type
employmentType.description: Select one or more applicable employment types.

experienceLevel.title: Experience Level
experienceLevel.description: Select one or more applicable experience levels.

salary.title: Salary Filter
salary.description: Filter by these salary ranges. Example: `100k+`

easyApply.title: LinkedIn Easy Apply
easyApply.description: Filter jobs with LinkedIn easy apply option.

postedLimit.title: Posted Limit
postedLimit.description: Filter jobs posted in the last hour, 24 hours, week or month.

industryIds.title: Industry IDs Filter
industryIds.description: Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn industry IDs. Example: `4` for 'Software Development'. Full list: `https://github.com/HarvestAPI/linkedin-industry-codes-v2/blob/main/linkedin_industry_code_v2_all_eng_with_header.csv`

functionIds.title: Function Filter
functionIds.description: Filter jobs by these LinkedIn job functions. Example: `eng` for 'Engineering'. Full list: { "acct": "Accounting / Auditing", "adm": "Administrative", "advr": "Advertising", "anls": "Analyst", "art": "Art / Creative", "bd": "Business Development", "cnsl": "Consulting", "cust": "Customer Service", "dsgn": "Design", "dist": "Distribution", "edu": "Education", "eng": "Engineering", "fin": "Finance", "genb": "General Business", "hcpr": "Healthcare Provider", "hr": "Human Resources", "it": "Information Technology", "lgl": "Legal", "mgmt": "Management", "mnfc": "Manufacturing", "mrkt": "Marketing", "othr": "Other", "prdm": "Product Management", "prod": "Production", "prjm": "Project Management", "pr": "Public Relations", "prch": "Purchasing", "qa": "Quality Assurance", "rsch": "Research", "sale": "Sales", "sci": "Science", "stra": "Strategy / Planning", "supl": "Supply Chain", "trng": "Training", "wrt": "Writing / Editing" }

sortBy.title: Sort By
sortBy.description: Sort the results by date or relevance.

geoIds.title: Geo IDs Filter
geoIds.description: Filter Jobs by these LinkedIn geo IDs. Example: `103644278`.

page.title: Start Page Number
page.description: Page number to start scraping from, up to 40. Each page contains 25 jobs, and LinkedIn returns at most 1000 jobs per search.

cookie.title: LinkedIn Cookies
cookie.description: Your LinkedIn cookies. You can export them via the browser extension [Cookie-Editor](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cookie-editor/hlkenndednhfkekhgcdicdfddnkalmdm/).
cookie.sectionDescription: Optionally, you can provide your LinkedIn cookie to use your session for scraping. This can help you get jobs in your region and those relevant to your account. Your account will only be used to scrape search pages; for job details we will use our resources.

userAgent.title: User Agent
userAgent.description: User agent to use for scraping. Copy your User Agent from https://www.whatismybrowser.com/detect/what-is-my-user-agent/ and paste it here.

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.description: Proxy URL to use for scraping. If not provided, the actor will use its default proxy. For safe scraping, we recommend you to find and provide a clean residential proxy.
